newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Prairies to see clouds, cool temperatures.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Prairies to see clouds, cool temperatures.

text.p: Canada's Prairies on Monday were forecast to see increasing cloudiness and cooler temperatures, Environment Canada said.
Trace amounts of rain fell on southeast Saskatchewan and southwest Manitoba in the last 24 hours. East central Alberta saw 10 mm of rain, meteorologist Steve Smith said.
An Arctic air mass was beginning to move into Alberta and should reach the south end of the province Monday evening.
Highs on the day should range between -8.0 Celsius in the north to 6.0 in central Alberta and 18 in the south.
Saskatchewan may see rain in the west and central areas.
Highs in Saskatchewan should range between -1.0 to 12 Celsius.
Manitoba should see increasing cloudiness with highs of 0 to 8.0 Celsius.
Harvest was virtually complete in Manitoba, 80 percent complete in Alberta and 89 percent done in Saskatchewan by last Monday, provincial agriculture reports said.
